title: Subject Vocabulary core scheme
description: Seven abilities a person using the product can rely on, and one internal concept for how the product itself is built. Every adopting repository shares them; each adds its own themes and components underneath. ISO/IEC 25010:2023 matches are informative and cite the characteristic name only.

concepts.definition: Your documents follow an agreed lifecycle: each has an owner, the right people sign off, and its metadata stays valid as it moves from draft to archived.
concepts.scopeNote: Lifecycles, sign-off, policies, registers and front-matter validity. Not how documents link to each other (traceability) or how they are found (discoverability). A narrower Authoring concept, ability:authoring, is reserved for a later version.

concepts.definition: You can follow any piece of work from the question that started it to the change that answered it.
concepts.scopeNote: Identifiers, links, lineage and history. Not search or navigation (discoverability).

concepts.definition: You can find the work you need, and move between related pieces, without knowing where it lives.
concepts.scopeNote: Search, filters, graph and board views, and navigation. Not a summary of the state of work (observability).

concepts.definition: You can see the state of all your work at a glance, and notice when something stalls.
concepts.scopeNote: Dashboards, metrics, reports, status roll-ups and health. Not finding one particular item (discoverability).

concepts.definition: It works with the tools and agents you already use, through open formats and documented interfaces.
concepts.scopeNote: APIs, MCP tools, file formats, exports and agent integrations. Not how the product itself is built and released (engineering quality).

concepts.definition: It is safe by default: secrets, credentials and access are protected, and risky actions ask before they act.
concepts.scopeNote: Threats, secrets, access control, vulnerable dependencies and safe defaults. Not whether document metadata is valid (governability).

concepts.definition: Your branches, worktrees and stashes stay tidy, and merged work is cleaned up without losing anything.
concepts.scopeNote: Branch, worktree and stash management and clean-up. Not the documents inside the repository (governability).

concepts.definition: The product itself is tested, releasable, maintainable and fast.
concepts.scopeNote: Tests, continuous integration, releases, packaging, refactoring and performance of the product. Internal: customer-facing views may hide it.
